stories.title: CISA Warns of 4 Exploited Flaws Linked to Ransomware, Cryptomining, and LLMjacking Attacks
stories.abstract: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include five actively exploited flaws affecting Synology DSM, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, REDCap, and Perforce Puppet Enterprise. These vulnerabilities facilitate various malicious activities, including ransomware deployment and unauthorized system access.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be under active exploitation, posing a high risk of compromise for organizations utilizing the affected software.
stories.action: Patch Synology DSM, LiteLLM, Apache Axis, REDCap, and Puppet Enterprise immediately.

stories.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
stories.abstract: Palo Alto Networks confirmed active exploitation of two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, affecting PAN-OS management interfaces. These flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution, enabling attackers to compromise exposed firewall management consoles.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities allow full system compromise of perimeter security devices, and they are currently being exploited in the wild.
stories.action: Restrict management interface access and apply vendor patches immediately.

stories.title: PHP Fixes 7 Critical Flaws, Including Bugs That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
stories.abstract: The PHP development team has released security patches addressing 18 vulnerabilities. The update resolves several critical remote code execution flaws, including issues related to session handling that could allow unauthenticated attackers to compromise servers by executing arbitrary code with worker process privileges.
stories.why: Unauthenticated RCE vulnerabilities in core server-side languages pose a high risk for full system compromise and lateral movement within infrastructure.
stories.action: Update PHP installations to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Siemens Industrial Software Products
stories.abstract: Siemens has identified that several industrial software products are vulnerable to the Node2Shell flaw (CVE-2026-111497). This critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the bundled Brotli decoder could allow remote attackers to corrupt memory or execute arbitrary code on affected systems.
stories.why: The vulnerability is actively exploited and poses a high risk of remote code execution within industrial environments.
stories.action: Review Siemens security bulletins and update affected software to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
stories.abstract: CISA has added a critical remote code execution vulnerability in Perforce Puppet to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-115731, is currently being actively targeted by threat actors to compromise enterprise infrastructure management servers.
stories.why: Successful exploitation allows attackers to gain unauthorized control over configuration management systems, potentially leading to widespread infrastructure compromise.
stories.action: Patch Perforce Puppet instances immediately.

stories.title: VMware security advisory (AV26-1185)
Oracle to Patch 11 Java Flaws Today as Critical OpenJDK RCE (CVE-2026-114938) Report Emerges
stories.abstract: A critical heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability, identified as CVE-2026-114938, affects the Base64 library within OpenJDK. This flaw allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on systems running vulnerable Java applications.
stories.why: The vulnerability poses a high risk of remote code execution in widely deployed Java environments, potentially leading to full system compromise.
stories.action: Apply vendor-provided patches for OpenJDK and affected Java applications immediately.

stories.title: Newly Patched VMware vCenter Flaw Exploited as Zero-Day by Chinese APT
stories.abstract: A China-aligned threat actor leveraged a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in VMware vCenter as a zero-day exploit. The flaw allowed unauthorized access to internal systems before Broadcom issued a security update to address the underlying weakness.
stories.why: State-sponsored actors are actively targeting virtualization infrastructure to gain persistent access and facilitate espionage within enterprise environments.
stories.action: Update VMware vCenter to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: TfL takes Oyster photocard website offline after attackers compromise customer accounts
stories.abstract: Transport for London confirmed a security incident involving its Oyster photocard system, potentially exposing personal account information for approximately 265,000 customers. The breach was identified after unauthorized emails were distributed to users through the agency's official communication channels.
stories.why: Unauthorized access to public infrastructure databases often leads to downstream phishing campaigns targeting affected users with highly personalized lures.

stories.title: NVIDIA investigating Gentlemen ransomware breach claims
stories.abstract: Nvidia is currently investigating claims of a security breach after the Gentlemen ransomware group listed the company on its extortion portal. The hardware manufacturer reports that internal reviews have not yet uncovered any evidence of a successful system compromise.
stories.why: Ransomware groups often use high-profile claims to gain leverage or credibility, necessitating verification of internal logs and access controls.

stories.title: Black Hat USA 2026 | GPUBreach: Privilege Escalation Attacks on GPUs Using Rowhammer
stories.abstract: Researchers have developed GPUBreach, a technique that weaponizes Rowhammer attacks against NVIDIA GPUs. By reverse-engineering page table allocation, attackers can induce deterministic bit flips to achieve cross-process memory access and full-system privilege escalation, moving beyond simple machine learning model degradation.
stories.why: This demonstrates a new, critical attack surface for GPU-accelerated environments, potentially allowing unprivileged code to compromise system-level memory protections.

stories.title: Drupal security advisory (AV26-1186)
stories.abstract: The Cyber Centre has issued alerts for critical vulnerabilities in Drupal core, Mitel MiCollab, and various PHP versions. These flaws include a remote code execution risk in Drupal, necessitating immediate attention from administrators to secure their respective environments against potential exploitation.
stories.why: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in core frameworks and enterprise communication platforms pose significant risks for unauthorized system access and data compromise.
stories.action: Update Drupal to 10.6.22, 11.3.22, or 11.4.13; patch PHP and MiCollab to the latest versions.

stories.title: CISA nominee LoSapio vows to bolster cyber defenses while denying Jan. 6 Capitol attack
stories.abstract: President-elect Trump has nominated a new CISA director who has committed to auditing the agency for operational deficiencies. During confirmation proceedings, the nominee sparked controversy by disputing the characterization of the January 6 Capitol riot as an attack.
stories.why: Leadership changes at CISA impact federal cybersecurity strategy, critical infrastructure protection priorities, and the agency's overall political independence.

stories.title: European Commission confirms cyberattack, says hackers used AI tool
stories.abstract: The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack targeting specific internal systems. Investigators identified the use of ARTEX, an open-source AI-powered hacking framework recently flagged by the FBI as a tool favored by both state-sponsored actors and cybercriminal syndicates.
stories.why: The adoption of AI-driven offensive toolkits by sophisticated threat actors lowers the barrier to entry for complex, automated exploitation of enterprise networks.

stories.title: Scans for LiteLLM/Starlette (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710), (Mon, Nov 16th)
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively scanning for vulnerabilities in LiteLLM and Starlette, specifically targeting endpoints associated with CVE-2026-42271 and CVE-2026-48710. These flaws can be chained to facilitate unauthenticated remote code execution.
stories.why: Exploitation allows attackers to gain full system control without credentials, posing a critical risk to infrastructure running these frameworks.
stories.action: Patch LiteLLM and Starlette instances immediately to the latest secure versions.

stories.title: How to Tell If It’s a Cyberattack or Just an Outage
stories.abstract: Recent high-profile service disruptions across critical infrastructure have fueled public speculation regarding cyberattacks. Security experts emphasize that most widespread outages stem from technical errors, misconfigurations, or software bugs rather than malicious state-sponsored or criminal hacking campaigns.
stories.why: Distinguishing between routine technical failures and targeted attacks prevents misallocation of incident response resources and avoids unnecessary panic during service outages.

stories.title: Elecbrakes EB2, VM1, ELBC2000
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in Elecbrakes EB2, VM1, and ELBC2000 trailer brake controllers allow attackers to bypass authentication, modify firmware, and manipulate safety-critical functions like braking and lighting. These flaws pose significant risks to vehicle operation and road safety.
stories.why: Remote manipulation of trailer braking systems presents a severe physical safety risk and potential for kinetic impact.
stories.action: Update EB2 to version 3.0.4.2.1 or later and VM1 to 1.3.4.2.1 or later.

stories.title: libumqtt
stories.abstract: The libumqtt library, versions 1.1.1 and earlier, contains an integer underflow vulnerability. Remote attackers can exploit this flaw to trigger memory corruption, disclose sensitive information, or crash the application through a denial-of-service condition.
stories.why: This library is utilized across critical infrastructure sectors, making it a potential target for remote exploitation in industrial and IT environments.

stories.title: Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime
stories.abstract: A race condition in Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime versions 4.2.4 and earlier enables attackers to bypass account existence checks. By sending concurrent requests, unauthenticated users can successfully create multiple administrative accounts within the system.
stories.why: This flaw allows unauthorized privilege escalation in industrial control systems, potentially granting attackers full administrative access to critical infrastructure environments.
stories.action: Update Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime to a version beyond 4.2.4.

stories.title: Ukraine exposes ransomware network extorting US oil, healthcare firms
stories.abstract: Ukrainian law enforcement, in coordination with the FBI, apprehended four individuals allegedly operating an international ransomware syndicate. The group is accused of extorting over $40 million from at least 28 global organizations, including entities within the American healthcare and energy sectors.
stories.why: This highlights the ongoing success of international law enforcement cooperation in dismantling high-impact ransomware operations targeting critical infrastructure.

stories.title: Cyberattack on service provider exposes payee data at 40 Irish credit unions
stories.abstract: Wellington IT, a technology provider for Irish credit unions, suffered a significant data breach in October. The incident exposed sensitive personal information belonging to members across 50 credit unions, with officials criticizing the company for failing to disclose the compromise in a timely manner.
stories.why: Supply chain compromises at critical financial service providers create systemic risks for downstream institutions and their customer data privacy.

stories.title: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
stories.abstract: A decade-old remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-123007, has been identified in NGINX's HTTP/2 implementation. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code within the NGINX worker process. Patches are available in versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7.
stories.why: This critical vulnerability affects a widely deployed web server component and permits unauthenticated remote code execution, posing a significant risk to infrastructure.
stories.action: Update NGINX to version 1.31.9 or 1.30.7 immediately.

stories.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
stories.abstract: A race condition in PHP's default session storage mechanism allows attackers to inject arbitrary objects by interrupting session write operations. When paired with existing application gadget chains, this vulnerability enables remote code execution on the underlying server.
stories.why: This flaw facilitates remote code execution by manipulating session data, potentially leading to full server compromise in applications with vulnerable object deserialization paths.
stories.action: Update PHP to the latest patched version.

stories.title: Attackers Compromise Microsoft's Agent Framework PyPI Package to Steal Cloud Credentials
stories.abstract: Attackers compromised a Microsoft GitHub account to inject malicious code into the official agent-framework Python package on PyPI. Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 were weaponized to exfiltrate cloud credentials and sensitive data from developer environments upon execution.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting official packages bypass standard trust models, potentially compromising developer workstations and cloud infrastructure environments.
stories.action: Audit environments for agent-framework versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 and rotate any exposed cloud credentials.

stories.title: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
stories.abstract: Security researchers have identified five key indicators of compromise that typically precede ransomware deployment. These early warning signs include unauthorized credential access, lateral network movement, and deliberate efforts by attackers to neutralize security software before data exfiltration or encryption occurs.
stories.why: Recognizing these pre-encryption behaviors allows security teams to disrupt the attack lifecycle before the final, destructive phase of a ransomware incident.

stories.title: Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and More
stories.abstract: A critical memory-corruption vulnerability, CVE-2026-114938, affects OpenJDK versions 17.0.6 and later. The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution on x86-64 systems utilizing AVX-512 VBMI instructions, impacting widely deployed enterprise software including Jira, Jenkins, and Keycloak.
stories.why: This vulnerability enables pre-authentication RCE on critical infrastructure and identity management platforms, posing a significant risk to enterprise environments.
stories.action: Update OpenJDK to the latest patched version immediately, prioritizing internet-facing applications.

stories.title: To Catch a Ransomware Scammer, FBI Posed as Both Victim and Attacker
stories.abstract: Federal agents successfully apprehended a suspected fraudster by orchestrating a sting operation where they impersonated both the targeted victim and the ransomware operators involved in the extortion attempt.
stories.why: This demonstrates sophisticated law enforcement tradecraft in disrupting ransomware ecosystems through active deception and tactical impersonation.

stories.title: Nvidia adds possible hack to list of very bad things under investigation
stories.abstract: Nvidia is currently investigating a potential data breach after a ransomware syndicate claimed to have compromised the company's internal systems. The threat actors have issued an ultimatum, threatening to publish stolen proprietary information if their financial demands remain unmet.
stories.why: Large-scale exfiltration of intellectual property from a major semiconductor firm poses significant risks to supply chain integrity and competitive security.

stories.title: F5 security advisory (AV26-1178)
Hackers Exploit Cisco Expressway Vulnerability Soon After PoC Release
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively exploiting a vulnerability in Cisco Expressway clusters. Following the publication of proof-of-concept code, attackers successfully compromised a Russian organization and established infrastructure to facilitate lateral movement within the network.
stories.why: This indicates rapid weaponization of public exploits against enterprise collaboration infrastructure, posing a significant risk of unauthorized network access and internal reconnaissance.
stories.action: Review Cisco security advisories and apply available patches for Expressway devices immediately.

stories.title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw That Could Give Unauthenticated Attackers Control of Sites
stories.abstract: Drupal has addressed a critical vulnerability in its core installer that could permit unauthenticated attackers to trigger a site reinstallation. This flaw potentially enables remote code execution and full site takeover, though the specific conditions required for exploitation are considered rare.
stories.why: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in core CMS frameworks pose a severe risk of total infrastructure compromise and data exfiltration.
stories.action: Update Drupal core to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks
stories.abstract: Apache has issued patches for a critical vulnerability in Roller that is currently being exploited by threat actors to achieve remote code execution. Additionally, attackers are actively targeting Confluence Data Center installations by leveraging a separate security flaw within the Axis framework.
stories.why: Active exploitation of remote code execution vulnerabilities in server-side software poses a severe risk of full system compromise and data exfiltration.
stories.action: Update Apache Roller to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: UK government forced to disclose secret Apple backdoor order
stories.abstract: A UK tribunal ruled that the government must disclose a previously secret order issued to Apple regarding encryption. The court rejected official claims that revealing the mandate would compromise national security, forcing transparency on state-level demands for access to encrypted communications.
stories.why: It highlights the legal mechanisms governments use to compel tech companies to undermine encryption, impacting trust in platform security and privacy guarantees.

stories.title: European Commission scrambles to contain AI-assisted cyberattack
stories.abstract: The European Commission has suspended its HR and medical reimbursement portals following a suspected cyberattack. Officials are currently investigating the incident to determine if sensitive employee information was accessed or exfiltrated during the breach.
stories.why: Large-scale government data breaches involving personnel records present significant risks for identity theft, targeted phishing, and long-term espionage against public sector employees.

stories.title: Russian COLD RELIC Hackers Use Stolen Google Workspace Data to Breach Second U.S. Organization
stories.abstract: The Russian-linked threat actor Cold Relic is leveraging data exfiltrated from initial cloud compromises to launch sophisticated, multi-stage social engineering campaigns. By impersonating trusted contacts, the group uses stolen information to facilitate subsequent intrusions against third-party organizations.
stories.why: This demonstrates a shift toward using stolen cloud data to weaponize trust, complicating detection for organizations relying on standard identity verification.

stories.title: Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation, No Authentication Required
stories.abstract: Apache Roller is currently facing active exploitation of a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-129448, stems from insecure deserialization within the platform's XML-RPC endpoint, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code without needing valid credentials.
stories.why: Unauthenticated RCE in a web-facing application represents a severe risk of full system compromise and lateral movement within the network.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches from Apache immediately.

stories.title: Java4Shell, NGINX2Shell and more: Why we are not at "Yellow", (Wed, Nov 18th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center reports a recent surge in critical vulnerabilities, including issues affecting Java and NGINX, alongside a major Microsoft 365 outage. Despite this cluster of high-impact events, the organization has opted to maintain its current Infocon threat level.
stories.why: Multiple concurrent critical vulnerabilities and service outages increase the attack surface and potential for exploitation across enterprise environments.

stories.title: Europe's biggest gas supplier battling cyberattack – with no timeline for recovery
stories.abstract: Norwegian energy company Equinor is currently managing a cyberattack affecting its internal systems. While the firm confirms that its primary oil and gas production operations remain stable and fully functional, there is currently no estimated timeframe for a complete recovery of the impacted infrastructure.
stories.why: Energy sector infrastructure is a high-value target for state-sponsored actors, making operational disruptions a significant concern for critical infrastructure security.

stories.title: Cisco security advisory (AV26-1175)
stories.abstract: Cisco has released security updates for its Secure Endpoint Connector across Linux, macOS, and Windows platforms. These patches address vulnerabilities stemming from integrated ClamAV components, necessitating version upgrades to maintain the integrity of endpoint protection services.
stories.why: Unpatched endpoint security agents can be exploited to bypass local defenses or facilitate privilege escalation on managed systems.
stories.action: Update Secure Endpoint Connector to versions 1.29.3 (Linux), 1.27.5 (Mac), or 8.6.4 (Windows).

stories.title: ThreatsDay: GPT-6.2 Jailbreak Flaws, BubbleLoader PNG Malware, $500M Ransom Demands + 17 More Stories
stories.abstract: Recent security reports highlight a trend where attackers leverage common, expected interactions—such as fake job offers or service notifications—to facilitate data theft and malware distribution. Additionally, evolving AI capabilities are increasingly lowering the barrier to entry for executing these deceptive campaigns.
stories.why: Attackers are shifting toward high-context social engineering, making traditional signature-based detection less effective against personalized, believable lures.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Thursday, November 19th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10186, (Thu, Nov 19th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center's daily podcast provides a summary of current cybersecurity events and technical updates for security professionals, focusing on emerging threats and operational intelligence observed across the global threat landscape.
stories.why: Staying informed on daily threat telemetry helps security teams identify and mitigate emerging attack vectors before they impact organizational infrastructure.

stories.title: Treat Your Honeypot Analysis Like Code: Git, Pull Requests and a Human Gate for AI [Guest Diary], (Wed, Nov 18th)
stories.abstract: A SANS ISC guest diary proposes treating honeypot analysis workflows like software development. By utilizing Git version control, pull requests, and human oversight for AI-generated insights, security teams can improve the reliability and auditability of their threat intelligence gathering processes.
stories.why: Standardizing honeypot data analysis through code-based workflows reduces human error and improves the quality of automated threat detection.

stories.title: New EggStreme Malware Variant Goes Silent to Evade Security Tools in Government Attacks
stories.abstract: A Chinese-linked threat actor has overhauled its EggStreme malware toolkit and infrastructure to bypass security detection. The group continues to target Philippine government entities, utilizing frequent recompilation and infrastructure rotation to maintain persistence and evade identification by security software.
stories.why: This demonstrates how APT groups rapidly evolve their TTPs and infrastructure to maintain access after being publicly exposed by security researchers.

stories.title: Google security advisory (AV26-1171)
stories.abstract: Google has released security updates for the Chrome desktop browser to address vulnerabilities affecting Windows, macOS, and Linux users. The patch applies to all versions preceding 158.0.8127.36 and 158.0.8127.37.
stories.why: Unpatched browser vulnerabilities are frequently exploited as entry points for remote code execution or sandbox escapes.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 158.0.8127.36 or higher.

stories.title: Rakuten Securities Breach Could Impact 15 Million Customers
stories.abstract: Rakuten Securities disclosed a significant data breach affecting approximately 15 million customers. The incident involved the unauthorized exposure of sensitive account information held by the Japanese brokerage firm.
stories.why: Large-scale financial data leaks increase the risk of targeted phishing, identity theft, and credential stuffing attacks against the affected user base.

stories.title: Oracle Corporation security advisory (AV26-1170)
stories.abstract: Oracle has released its quarterly security updates addressing numerous vulnerabilities across a wide range of products, including MySQL, Oracle APEX, and various enterprise management suites. Administrators should review the full list of affected software to identify necessary patches for their specific environments.
stories.why: Unpatched Oracle enterprise software is a frequent target for attackers seeking to gain unauthorized access or execute code within internal corporate networks.
stories.action: Review the Oracle Critical Patch Update advisory and apply relevant patches to affected systems.

stories.title: AI found more critical bugs in another widely used technology running 225M websites
stories.abstract: Researchers utilized artificial intelligence to identify five critical vulnerabilities within the NGINX web server. These flaws could potentially allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code and gain full control over affected infrastructure, impacting millions of websites globally.
stories.why: NGINX is a foundational component of the internet; remote code execution vulnerabilities in such widely deployed software pose significant systemic risk.
stories.action: Monitor NGINX security advisories and apply patches immediately upon release.

stories.title: Navigating Vulnerability Hysteria in the AI Era
stories.abstract: Recent high-severity vulnerability disclosures are causing significant operational strain. Security teams are struggling with widespread panic and alert fatigue, exacerbated by growing concerns that artificial intelligence will accelerate the development and deployment of sophisticated exploits.
stories.why: Excessive alarmism regarding AI-driven threats can distract security teams from prioritizing genuine, high-impact risks within their specific environments.

stories.title: Hackers Breach N-able Cloud Server, Disrupting Email Security Management Across 3 Regions
stories.abstract: N-able reported a security breach involving unauthorized access to a server within its Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud. The incident forced the company to temporarily disable management interfaces and APIs across three regions while they investigate and harden their infrastructure.
stories.why: Compromised cloud management infrastructure can lead to downstream configuration tampering or unauthorized access to sensitive email security settings for managed service providers.

stories.title: Dorsett Controls InfoScan
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities in Dorsett Controls InfoScan versions 1.45.0 and earlier expose water and wastewater infrastructure to risks including credential theft, unauthorized data access, and traffic interception due to hard-coded keys and authentication failures.
stories.why: These flaws allow attackers to compromise critical industrial control systems, potentially leading to unauthorized manipulation of water management processes.
stories.action: Update Dorsett Controls InfoScan to a version beyond 1.45.0.

stories.title: British hackers face prison for GTA 6 data breach and crypto thefts
stories.abstract: Two British individuals have been convicted for their roles in high-profile cyberattacks against Rockstar Games, the developer of Grand Theft Auto, and for orchestrating significant cryptocurrency thefts. Both defendants now await sentencing for these criminal activities.
stories.why: This case highlights the severe legal consequences for corporate data breaches and digital asset theft, serving as a deterrent for cybercriminal activity.

stories.title: UK court confirms British government served Apple with secret encryption notice
stories.abstract: A UK tribunal has officially confirmed that the British government issued a secret legal order compelling Apple to weaken cryptographic protections for iCloud accounts. This admission concludes a two-year period during which authorities refused to acknowledge the existence of the mandate.
stories.why: It highlights the ongoing tension between government surveillance requirements and the integrity of end-to-end encryption protocols used by major service providers.

stories.title: PHP Warns of Critical Security Flaws Affecting All Supported Versions, Fixes Coming November 19
stories.abstract: The PHP development team has announced an upcoming security update scheduled for November 19, 2026. This patch will address critical vulnerabilities impacting every currently supported version of the programming language.
stories.why: Unpatched critical vulnerabilities in PHP can lead to remote code execution, potentially compromising web servers and applications relying on the language.
stories.action: Prepare to update all PHP installations on November 19.

stories.title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked
stories.abstract: Major financial institutions, including Citi, are restricting the use of third-party AI agents to access customer accounts. Banks are signaling that they will not accept liability for unauthorized transactions or security breaches resulting from these automated financial tools.
stories.why: This shift in liability policies forces security teams to reconsider the risk profile of automated financial integrations and third-party data access.

stories.title: Mass Surveillance and GTA
stories.abstract: Internal documents reveal that ICE is compensating AT&T for access to massive volumes of call detail records. This arrangement provides the agency with analytical tools to parse trillions of records, raising significant concerns regarding privacy and the scope of government surveillance.
stories.why: It highlights the ease with which government agencies can bypass traditional warrant requirements by purchasing sensitive metadata directly from telecommunications providers.

stories.title: AttackIQ Research Reveals How Iranian Cyber Groups Hand Off Network Access to Enable Destructive Attacks
Siemens Mendix Studio Pro
stories.abstract: Siemens Mendix Studio Pro contains vulnerabilities in its MCP Server involving unrestricted IP binding and cross-site request forgery. These flaws could enable remote attackers to execute unauthorized commands, access sensitive data, or compromise the underlying system through malicious browser interactions.
stories.why: Exploitation allows unauthorized remote access and system control, posing significant risks to industrial environments utilizing the Mendix development platform.
stories.action: Update Mendix Studio Pro to version 11.16.0 or 11.12.7.

stories.title: Critical VMware vCenter Flaw (CVSS 9.8) Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication
Black Hat USA 2026 | Can AI Do Novel Security Research? Meet the HTTP Terminator
DOJ, DHS partner on new unit tackling scams and cybercrime
